title: Isaiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 33
description: Ten questions on Isaiah 33: woe to the destroyer, who can live with the devouring fire, and Yahweh our judge, lawgiver and king.

questions.text: What will happen to the destroyer when he has finished destroying?
questions.explanation: Woe to you who destroy but weren't destroyed: when you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed, and when you have finished betrayal, you will be betrayed.

answers.text: He will flee to a distant land

questions.text: What does the prayer ask Yahweh to be every morning?
questions.explanation: The prayer is: "Be our strength every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble."

questions.text: What do the ambassadors of peace do?
questions.explanation: Their valiant ones cry outside, and the ambassadors of peace weep bitterly.

questions.text: What is said about Sharon when the land mourns?
questions.explanation: Lebanon is confounded and withers away, Sharon is like a desert, and Bashan and Carmel are stripped bare.

questions.text: What will the peoples be like, according to verse 12?
questions.explanation: The peoples will be like the burning of lime, like thorns that are cut down and burned in the fire.

answers.text: Like the burning of lime and thorns burned in the fire
Like chaff that is driven before the wind
Like wax melting away before the burning flames
Like grass that withers on the housetops

questions.text: What question follows when the sinners in Zion are afraid and trembling seizes the godless ones?
questions.explanation: After saying that the sinners in Zion are afraid, the verse asks, "Who among us can live with the devouring fire? Who among us can live with everlasting burning?"

answers.text: "Where can we flee from his presence?"
"Who among us can live with the devouring fire?"
"Who will deliver us from the enemy?"

questions.text: What is promised to the one who walks righteously and speaks blamelessly?
questions.explanation: He will dwell on high; his place of defense will be the fortress of rocks, his bread will be supplied, and his waters will be sure.

answers.text: He will live to see his children's children
He will receive the nations for his inheritance
He will dwell on high, and his bread will be supplied
He will eat forever at the king's own table

questions.text: How is Jerusalem described when your eyes look at Zion?
questions.explanation: Jerusalem will be a quiet habitation, a tent that won't be removed; its stakes will never be plucked up, nor any of its cords broken.

answers.text: A fortress with high towers of iron
A city set on a hill that cannot be hidden
A garden enclosed behind high walls
A tent that won't be removed

questions.text: Which three titles does verse 22 give to Yahweh?
questions.explanation: The verse says: "Yahweh is our judge. Yahweh is our lawgiver. Yahweh is our king. He will save us."

questions.text: What will the inhabitant not say?
questions.explanation: The inhabitant won't say, "I am sick," and the people who dwell there will be forgiven their iniquity.
